findings.title: Architecture principles are faithfully implemented
findings.description: The design upholds every load-bearing architectural principle from 400-arch. "Measure, never gate" is honored by the explicit exclusion of gates, pipeline hooks, and composite scores (Excluded list). "Extend the 320 store, don't fork it" is met via the `slice_ranges` optional sibling payload on `MetrologyRecord` with `schema_version` unchanged and existing records loading unchanged (Database/Storage Schema). "Absent is not zero" is maintained through `environment_unresolved`, `RangeUnresolvedReason`, and `ComparabilityBreak` enums. "Breakdown, not a score" is enforced by a test asserting no serialized report key contains `score` (D8, criterion 9). "Normalize categories, not severities" is respected — review severity stays on the review scale only (D8). "Coarse records" is followed by the one-record-per-project `SliceRanges` design (D1).

findings.title: Slice plan scope and success criteria are fully covered
findings.description: Every success criterion from the slice plan entry (400-slices, item 4) maps to a functional criterion in the design. Durable ranges from topology (criterion 1–3), commit export without writing to `.git` with lockfile-gated type counts (criterion 4–6), full-identity-match comparability with named breaks (criterion 7, D7), LLM-sourced noise-floor display and sample sizes (criterion 8–9, D8), and unresolved-slice project-level-only attribution (criterion 10, D9) all have explicit coverage. The dependency list matches ([400, 402]) and the interface contract matches the plan's "Provides slice-range record type, commit export, and report commands; Consumes snapshot, review, audit and noise-floor records, and review/git_utils.py."

findings.title: Integration points match consuming and providing slice contracts
findings.description: The 402 contract is consumed correctly: `None` category is treated as missing (not `other`), `read_side_mapped` records are labeled as separate columns (D8), and records without `slice_index` roll up at project level only (D9). This matches 402's "Provides to Other Slices" section exactly. The 420 interface provides `take_snapshot_at(commit)` and `get_slice_ranges` for slice boundaries and own commits (`fork..tip`), which is what the architecture's "Envisioned State" says 420 needs. The `environment_root` contract change to `AdapterContext` is minimal (one required field, in-place sets it equal to `repo_root`), justified by the architecture's "A snapshot measures a commit" principle, and the design explicitly notes 400's tests pass unchanged with `environment_root == repo_root`.

findings.title: Failure modes comprehensively enumerated for all new I/O paths
findings.description: The failure-mode table covers every new I/O path: `git archive`/`rev-parse` failure and hang (timeout at 30s via `run_git`), extraction `OSError`, unknown revisions, `data` filter refusals, tool hangs inside exports (bounded by existing `snapshot_tool_timeout_s`), boundary snapshot failures during reports (stop, no half before/after), reflog/merge search returning `None` (try next path, never empty range), stored landings with missing commits (`git cat-file -e` check, WARNING, other landings still reported), concurrent writes (last-write-wins, re-resolvable), and store write failures. Each has an explicit handling strategy and signal — no "TBD" or implicit handling.

findings.title: Proportionality is appropriate for a 4/5 effort slice
findings.description: The included scope (range resolver, commit export, three report commands, comparability module, one contract field) directly maps to the slice plan's stated deliverables. The excluded list is explicit and defensible: no audits/reviews from reports, no review noise floor, no dependency installation, no composite scores, no slice table in `report project` (no criterion needs it). The 10 technical decisions each address a real design question (multiple landings, sync-merge false positives, before/after definition, ahead-of-need persistence, export tool resolution, lockfile gating, per-measurement comparability, noise-floor states, attribution rules, command placement). The module count (~16 modules) is reasonable for the scope, and the design constrains new modules to ~300 lines and `git_utils.py` growth to only the rename, pattern function, and `first_parent` argument.

findings.title: Settings-in-slice blind spot is acknowledged, not hidden
findings.description: The design explicitly calls out in its Risk Assessment that a slice which edits `.squadron.toml` settings won't show `limits_changed` or `exclusions_changed` between two exports, because both boundaries are measured under the live checkout's settings (D5). This is a known limitation of the "read settings from live checkout" approach, not a hidden dependency. The architecture doesn't require detecting in-slice settings changes, and the design states each record records which settings it used. This is correctly characterized as a risk with a stated mitigation (breaks fire against earlier snapshots taken under different settings), so no action is required.

structured_findings.summary: Slice plan scope and success criteria are fully covered
Integration points match consuming and providing slice contracts
Failure modes comprehensively enumerated for all new I/O paths
Proportionality is appropriate for a 4/5 effort slice
Settings-in-slice blind spot is acknowledged, not hidden
